selection_basis: EDA-derived question coverage, evidence hierarchy, healthy or trained population transferability, and structured PMC full-text availability

selected.study_type: position stand and overview of reviews
selected.reason: Current ACSM synthesis anchors definitions, prescription variables, and evidence limitations.
Broad evidence synthesis directly maps prescription variables to strength and hypertrophy outcomes.
Compares combinations of load, sets, and frequency across a large randomized-trial network.
Models dose-response relationships and outcome specificity across strength and conditioning studies.

selected.population: healthy adults with mixed training status
selected.reason: Separates load effects on maximal strength from hypertrophy under volitional-failure protocols.
Provides a structured comparison of hypertrophy-related prescription variables.
Focused evidence on moderate versus high weekly volume in trained participants.
Primary study directly tests weekly set volume in a trained population.
Contrasts high-volume and high-load training with both strength and hypertrophy outcomes.
Directly evaluates frequency and volume-equated strength outcomes.
Addresses transferability of frequency findings to trained populations and in-season maintenance.
Volume-equated comparison of two versus four weekly sessions.

selected.population: young adults with mixed training status
selected.reason: Core synthesis of failure versus non-failure training with volume and training-status moderators.

selected.population: healthy adults with mixed training status
selected.reason: Clarifies inconsistent failure definitions and proximity-to-failure evidence.
Documents methodological limitations in periodized versus non-periodized comparisons.
Evaluates autoregulated progression against fixed loading for maximal strength.
Provides current operational definitions of resistance exercise and progressive overload.
Covers advanced techniques proposed for progression and plateau contexts while exposing evidence gaps.

selected.population: strength and physique sport coaches and athletes
selected.reason: Defines applied deload practice and makes the limited empirical evidence explicit.
Directly tests a one-week training cessation period within supervised resistance training.
Synthesizes mechanisms, time course, and prevention considerations for athlete detraining.
Quantifies residual effects after training cessation and documents population limitations.
